objects.summary: Owner starts Issue #44 as an execution mission: reconstruct existing VM/GPT-OSS worker/scheduler first, preserve REUSE > CONNECT > REPAIR > BUILD, implement only a proven missing seam, then attempt the real bounded GPT-OSS->GitHub->Codex->GitHub->GPT-OSS loop.

Repository-first reconstruction finds durable research worker/runtime primitives but cannot establish that the current container is the deployed VM or has GitHub/model/scheduler identity. It stops speculative implementation at UNKNOWN_PENDING_VM_EVIDENCE; targeted runtime tests and full suite pass with correct PYTHONPATH.

Owner challenges durability because local 4cebe57/branch are not remotely resolvable and requires the complete mission receipt/evidence request in Issue #44 itself, with remote persistence explicitly blocked if necessary.
Codex persists the read-only VM evidence request and admits remote publication is blocked by no remote/unauthenticated gh. Local SHA 96c54d6... is not represented as durable remote evidence.

Owner corrects the sequence: historical Control Tower/Edge Lab evidence must be exhausted before fresh VM evidence. Exact worker/scheduler/event/commit/run anchors are supplied for verification and scientific Edge Lab state must not be repurposed as project-management state.

Codex creates an additive historical-audit checkpoint but cannot fetch required primary refs due HTTP 403; honest verdict remains HISTORICAL_AUDIT_EXHAUSTED=FALSE_BLOCKED_PRIMARY_REFS_UNAVAILABLE. Local 77f7abc... is not remote durability.

GitHub-side bridge verifies exact Edge Lab head 68bbab8..., worker 6ac978ec..., configuration/run events, prompt hash, hourly Europe/Paris schedule, direct-launch 404 contradiction, historical commit bf8eef..., scheduled session and hosted run 38161433072 success. Current VM/model/write/dispatch remain unproven.

Owner corrects blocker taxonomy: CODEX_CONTAINER_GIT_FETCH=BLOCKED_403 is not project-global evidence absence. STATE/CHECKPOINT remote evidence proves one completed scheduled session while delivery_verified and unattended_independence_verified remain false.

Verified remote README/CONTROL/CHECKPOINT evidence proves the existing scheduler is reused, timer activation differs from worker liveness, one wake was observed, model/token identity is not established, and Control Tower Oct-30 reconciliation remains unpublished.

Remote bridge adds CONTROL.json blob identity and exact budget/capital settings plus historical wake diff/run details, again preserving UNKNOWN for current runtime/model/permanent daemon and current GitHub/Codex capabilities.

Codex consumes the bridge and narrows residual gap to current runtime/model, current liveness/schedule, GitHub write identity and real Codex dispatch/result observation. Next lawful action is read-only runtime/permissions probing; local a4bfe183... is not remotely proven.

Historical audit explains why delivery/unattended remain false: no causally bound delivery receipt, one wake only, unknown trigger attribution and no closed-chat continuation. Model/runtime/write/dispatch stay UNKNOWN; local a5be440... remains non-durable.

Codex identifies the residual seam as an authenticated, idempotent, causally fenced GitHub/Codex orchestration adapter rather than another scheduler. It documents minimum semantics but does not yet prove current runtime or remote durability.

Historical checkpoint keeps model identity explicitly UNKNOWN and reduces residual gap to present runtime/service, GitHub principal/permissions, Codex dispatch/result primitive, recovery/fencing and repeated closed-chat continuation. Local b94a70... not remote.

Owner establishes continuation law: Issue #44 must continue across subproblems and stop only at DONE, TRUE_HARD_BOUNDARY or globally PROVEN_EXTERNAL_BLOCK; UNKNOWN, local 403, push failure, lane block or important decisions are not terminal.

Continuation relaunch forbids repeating historical audit absent decision-changing facts and orders exhaustive search for remaining runtime/GitHub/dispatch evidence, then minimal connection if the seam is proven; local-only SHA is never durability.

Codex builds an isolated local orchestration sidecar with durable identities, fencing, retry, causal receipt validation and exact-SHA result qualification. Local tests pass, but real hosted loop cannot run and local 13928cf... is not remote evidence.

Codex declares PROVEN_EXTERNAL_BLOCK from its container after exhausting local runtime/network/credential surfaces, while preserving historical evidence and fail-closed science. The conclusion is later corrected as environment-local rather than target-architecture terminal.

Owner architecture correction makes the existing GPT-OSS/VM worker the persistent wake orchestrator, disables ChatGPT watcher as target, provides fresh RECOVERY_NEEDED/inactive telemetry and orders the sidecar to become a minimal adapter consumed by the existing worker with separately qualified dispatch/readback/unattended gates.

cross_object_findings.finding: Issue #44 initially moved too quickly to fresh VM evidence. Durable Control Tower history already proved scheduler/worker identity, prompt hash and one wake; exhausting it first materially narrowed the residual gap and avoided unnecessary runtime intervention.

Repeated container fetch/auth failures were not project-wide evidence absence because the connected GitHub side could recover exact refs. Block taxonomy matters for continuing useful work rather than returning control prematurely.

Historical scheduler/README evidence proves a worker wake but not GPT-OSS/Ollama/model identity. The target architecture may intend GPT-OSS, but historical execution identity remains UNKNOWN without primary runtime proof.

Multiple local checkpoints were created then lost/unpublished while the mission repeatedly returned after partial results. The continuation law explicitly targets this fragmentation by forbidding return on nonterminal UNKNOWN/local blockers.

After historical recovery, the missing connection is narrowed to authenticated/idempotent/causally fenced GitHub-Codex dispatch/readback from the existing worker. The Owner explicitly rejects substituting a new scheduler or ChatGPT watcher.
